column1: # THE BUBBLE COUPLING (PLAN item 32, 2026-09-24; the depth weight 2026-10-23): the record's own
# reading of `bubbleCouplingOf` / `bubble_coupling_of` -- the 3-year log run-up into the peaks of the
# series' deep declines, each weighted by its depth, less the mean 3-year log run-up at every
# all-time high, so a positive reading says the deep declines followed larger run-ups than a typical
# high did.  A peak is a session at a new all-time high (ties included) opening a spell; the spell's
# weight rises linearly in log depth from 0 at a 30% decline to 1 at 50% (`BUBBLE_RAMP_LOG`), so no
# single decline near a cut decides the row.  The last spell counts, censored at the series' end; a
# peak or a high without three years of history behind it is skipped; with no weight at all the row
# is undefined.  `Anchors.bubbleCoupling` / `bubble_coupling` is the graded series' `record`, and a
# test per twin re-derives it.
# Graded as an EXTREME row: no block resampling keeps the structure the statistic measures, so the
# row is the record's percentile among single histories of its own length (`bubbleYears`), MISS
# outside 5-95, as the worst crash is.  Measured 2026-10-23 on the 0.25.0 recipes (seed 1, 200
# histories): IXIC+NDX at the 69th percentile of the Nasdaq's histories, CRSP at the 84th of the
# S&P's.
# Each set grades its own index's longest record (2026-10-03):
# nasdaq  IXIC+NDX, the splice: the Nasdaq Composite's daily log returns through 1985-10-01, the
#         Nasdaq-100's after (Yahoo Finance's ^IXIC and ^NDX closes; price indexes),
#         1971-02-08..2026-09-18.  QQQ's record starts 1999-03-10, nine years too late for a 3-year
#         run-up into the 2000-03 peak, and the consumer's rules were selected on the NDX from 1990,
#         so its NDX rows (1990-01-03..2026-09-18) are reported, not graded (`NASDAQ_REPORTED`).
# sp500   CRSP value-weighted US market total return from Ken French's
#         F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily over the century, the tail window: Mkt-RF + RF
#         compounded into an index without a leading 1.0, then its log returns.
# LAG-FREE: the computed indexes' daily returns through 1999-03-10 (the IXIC, the NDX, CRSP) are read
# with the stale-price lag removed, an MA(2) inversion fitted per calendar five-year block
# (`unlag_returns`, the IXIC and the NDX declared `-index`); `-recorded` reads them as printed.
# Re-read 2026-10-04 from published sources (Yahoo Finance's ^IXIC and ^NDX closes, Ken French's
# 202608 daily file) by the commands below: every row identical.
# TWO MORE EXTREME ROWS on the same windows (2026-09-27): `largest 3y run-up` (`runUp3yOf` /
# `run_up_3y_of`, the maximum log return over any 756 sessions) and `longest calm stretch`
# (`calmStretchOf` / `calm_stretch_of`, the most sessions in a row within 20% of the running peak).
# Measured 2026-09-27 on 2000 histories: the century's run-up (x2.39) sat below 99.9% of the S&P
# worlds' and its calm stretch (2190 sessions) below 98% -- the worlds made events the century
# never did; the NDX's read at the 88th and 30th.  `Anchors.runUp3y` / `calmStretch` are the
# graded series' records, checked by the same test.
# `variance ratio 250d` (2026-10-03): the window's 250-session variance ratio (`varianceRatio` /
# `variance_ratio`, phase-averaged), the record the variance-ratio profile's 250-session rung
# grades against (`VAR_RATIO_250_ERAS`).  The Nasdaq's era is the splice's; the S&P's century row
# is `persistence-2026-09-11.tsv`'s c1926 reading.
# The -yahoo files are `date,adj_close,dlog_adj_close` CSVs, one row a session, the first row the anchor.
# Generated by `rust/src/bin/record_bands.rs -coupling` (twin: `jsrc/recordBands.sc -coupling`):
#   record_bands -coupling -set nasdaq -series IXIC+NDX -yahoo <data>/IXIC.csv
#       -index <data>/IXIC.csv -index <data>/NDX.csv
#   record_bands -coupling -set nasdaq -series NDX -yahoo <data>/NDX.csv
#       -from 1990-01-03 -to 2026-09-18 -index <data>/NDX.csv
#   record_bands -coupling -set sp500 -series CRSP -french <data>/french/F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily.csv
# To read past the Nasdaq record's last date on its published proxy, Ken French's daily HiTec industry:

#       -column HiTec -at 2026-09-18 -to <French's last day>
